disclaimer: Synthetic example, generated for the event's scenarios - it does not come from any real system, record or person, and only illustrates how such a summary could look.

samples.name: Andrea Lindqvist, 24
samples.tagline: Type 1 diabetes, seen in a Paris emergency department
samples.scenario: A Swedish exchange student is brought into a Paris emergency department with runaway blood sugar. Her summary is complete and well coded, but the data behind it has gone stale: the last labs are eight months old and the follow-up that would have refreshed them was cancelled and never rebooked.
samples.horizon: Future scenario: under the EHDS Regulation, cross-border exchange of patient summaries is required from around 2029.

samples.name: Arne Bergström, 83
samples.tagline: Multimorbid, admitted after a fall in Copenhagen
samples.scenario: A Swedish pensioner falls while visiting his son in Denmark and needs surgery. Ten conditions, ten medicines including the anticoagulant apixaban, and a high-criticality penicillin allergy with anaphylaxis have to survive the border.
samples.horizon: Future scenario: under the EHDS Regulation, cross-border exchange of patient summaries is required from around 2029, and of lab results and discharge reports only from around 2031.

samples.name: Vilhelm "Ville" Söderberg, 13
samples.tagline: Difficult airway and immunosuppressed, in a Gothenburg emergency department
samples.scenario: A Stockholm boy with a rare craniofacial syndrome, a known difficult airway and juvenile spondyloarthritis on adalimumab and methotrexate arrives at Sahlgrenska with a chest infection and worsening breathing. The team that has never met him needs the airway plan, the last anaesthetic, the last doses and who to ring at Karolinska - before anyone reaches for a laryngoscope.
